items.stem: In Flutter's layout model, how is a widget's size ultimately determined?

options.text: Constraints flow down from the parent and the child sizes itself within them
options.rationale: Correct: parents pass constraints down, children choose a size within them, and size flows back up.

options.text: Each widget picks its size independently of its parent
options.rationale: A child must size within the constraints its parent gives.

options.text: Sizes are fixed at compile time
options.rationale: Layout is resolved at runtime based on constraints.

options.text: The root widget sets every child's exact pixels
options.rationale: The root passes constraints; children still choose within them.

items.explanation: Correct: parents pass constraints down, children choose a size within them, and size flows back up.

items.stem: Which TWO are true about Dart's sound null safety? (Select TWO)

options.text: A variable must be declared with ? to hold null
options.rationale: Correct: non-nullable is the default; ? opts a type into null.

options.text: The compiler can guarantee a non-nullable variable is never null
options.rationale: Correct: sound null safety lets the compiler rule out null for non-nullable types.

options.text: Adding ! removes the possibility of a runtime null error
options.rationale: ! asserts non-null and throws if the value is actually null.

options.text: Null safety only applies to local variables
options.rationale: It applies across fields, parameters and return types too.

items.explanation: Correct: non-nullable is the default; ? opts a type into null.

items.stem: Why should a Future passed to FutureBuilder usually be created outside the build method?

options.text: build can run many times, recreating the Future and refetching on each rebuild
options.rationale: Correct: creating it in build triggers a new request on every rebuild; create it once and store it.

options.text: FutureBuilder cannot accept a Future created in build
options.rationale: It can; the problem is repeated recreation.

options.text: Futures created in build never complete
options.rationale: They complete, but a new one starts each rebuild.
The request stays asynchronous regardless of where the Future is made.

items.explanation: Correct: creating it in build triggers a new request on every rebuild; create it once and store it.
